discovery: Theory and realization of the self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE) X-ray free-electron laser

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

motivation: The nominees laid the theoretical foundations of the high-gain free-electron laser operating by self-amplified spontaneous emission. Saldin (with Kondratenko) and Pellegrini (with Bonifacio and Narducci) showed that a relativistic electron beam in a long undulator can collectively amplify its own spontaneous radiation to saturation. Kim developed the gain and coherence theory that made the X-ray regime quantitatively predictable. Pellegrini proposed the X-ray FEL at the SLAC linac and championed it to realization. LCLS, FLASH, European XFEL, SACLA, SwissFEL and PAL-XFEL now deliver coherent, femtosecond X-ray pulses a billion times brighter than synchrotrons. These sources have opened new physics: nonlinear X-ray optics, ultrafast electronic and structural dynamics, time-resolved inelastic scattering, warm dense matter, and serial femtosecond crystallography. For spectroscopy and scattering, this is the most transformative instrument since the synchrotron. Its operation confirms the predicted collective instability with striking precision.
